ui.title: So, do we call?
ui.toast: A donation link goes here. I promise not to spend it on roaming.

yes.text: They watched your story three times. That is an invitation.
Texting is cowardice. Call.
Voice notes don’t count. It has to be live.
One call and everything is clear. Or worse.
3 a.m. is the most honest hour for a conversation.
They are definitely awake. Nobody sleeps anyway.
You still have 400 minutes on the plan. Don’t waste them.
If they don’t pick up, they simply didn’t hear it.
Mum said call more often. Mum never said who.
The ringing tone is already half a conversation.
They won’t call first. Someone has to be the adult.
You’ll call back once and then quit. Obviously.
The phone is already in your hand. The rest is paperwork.
Five minutes, tops. As always — two hours.
Silence in the chat means it’s time to call.
“Call me whenever you can” — and you can.
The number is still not deleted. That’s a sign.
You’ve already drafted the opening line. Don’t waste it.
Roaming is expensive, but pride costs more.
Excuse ready: “just checking whether you’re alive”.
They haven’t blocked you. So they’re waiting.
Bad signal means a reason to call again.
You’re not asking anything serious. Just hearing a voice.
A pocket dial doesn’t count. Do it on purpose.
One ring, then hang up. Starting is the hard part.
They’re staring at their phone too. Right now.
If you don’t call you’ll think about it until morning.
The silence is two years old. Time to ruin it.
You’re not a stalker. You just really want to talk.
They won’t recognise you right away. Even better.
Calling at 7:58 a.m. counts as caring.
Voicemail is a listener too. And it never interrupts.
You’ve dialled 80% of the number. Stopping is unfair.
Keep the video off. But call.
They liked a photo from 2019 yesterday. They’re ready.
You have exactly one reason. That is plenty.
A text can be reread. A voice can’t. Call.
What if they’re waiting for exactly your call. Happens.
Battery at 4%. So the call will be short.
You rehearsed the first sentence. Twice.
They’ll say “I was just thinking about you”. Possibly.
Unknown number? Then call from your own. Be brave.
The neighbours hear everything anyway. Give them material.
A minute on the phone is cheaper than a week of thinking.
They read it and said nothing. So they want a call.
You dialled and hung up. Now you owe an explanation.
A missed call from you is a message too.
“Hi, it’s me” — the rest writes itself.
Your earbuds are charged. Fate left you no excuses.
They called first once. Debts get repaid.
Phones were built for calling. Shocking news.
Your voice sounds better on the phone. Honestly.
No answer the first time? Call the third time.
Office hours are over, so you can be human now.
You won’t cry. Well, almost.
“Let’s talk later” — later has arrived.
The die has seen your unsent drafts. Just call.
Your mood is perfect right now. In an hour it won’t be.
A call can’t be edited. That’s exactly why it works.
Last time. Say it with me: last time.

no.text: Don’t call. Text. Or do nothing at all.
Nobody needs your voice today. Not even you.
The subscriber would rather not. Neither would the die.
Some things are better left unsaid out loud.
A 3 a.m. call isn’t a gesture, it’s a diagnosis.
Get some sleep. The number isn’t going anywhere.
No. And don’t call back “just to ask something”.
The phone was invented so you wouldn’t use it.
Whatever you want to say will sound silly tomorrow.
Let them call first. Just once.
The die says no. The die saw your weekend.
